note: The context file this tier hands the shared evaluator is ONE ARM's transcript, so a `plan-jq` witness here queries that transcript and an `evidence-jq` witness queries that arm's campaign evidence. These are the witnesses that hold on EITHER arm; the arm-specific ones live in `witnesses-exhaust.json` and `witnesses-capture.json` and are evaluated only against the arm they are about. Nothing here is disjoined over `.walk`: a witness that reads its default on the walk that did not run is an absent signal with no way to tell "nothing fired" from "my instrument was disconnected", and `run-ladder.sh` runs BOTH arms by default so that every witness in all three files bites on some transcript of every run.

witnesses.provenance: The verifier cohort-16's `found-two-source` row states for exactly this failure (tools/cohort/steps.tsv): a market compiled WITHOUT `--recovery-rungs` reads a ZERO recovery link and is a different market, so a zero link means the flag never reached the compiler. The address checked here is the RecoveryPolicyV2 record the FOUNDING published on chain, read out of the founding campaign's own evidence, not out of the input this tier compiled.

`dclutch-source`'s `relay_frame_roles_v1(RelayFrameKindV1::AdvanceRecovery)` declares the frame's positions, and the AdvanceRecovery frame the deployed Resolution program parses is 18 accounts wide. The driver builds its metas FROM those roles and never from a typed list; this counts what it built and compares it against the contract's own width, so a frame that grew or shrank on either side is caught rather than assumed. GREEN NOW, and the reason is a producer rather than a parameter: the campaign MINTS its own Pyth publication at the cluster's own block time (`pyth_lab_publication.rs`), so the market's window ends at the run's own hour and both legs fall due inside it, which is what lets an AdvanceRecovery frame be built at all. It was red for as long as the publication was frozen at the capture date, because one `WindowSpecV1.max_age_seconds` governs both the crank's admissibility and the publication's freshness and no value of one field satisfies both legs against a frozen capture.

witnesses.query: if ([.cranks[] | select(.observedUnixSeconds != null) | select(.observedUnixSeconds >= .started_unix_seconds)] | length) == ([.cranks[] | select(.observedUnixSeconds != null)] | length) then "chain-clock-inside-the-run" else "chain-clock-outside-the-run" end
witnesses.provenance: TWO INDEPENDENT CLOCKS. `started_unix_seconds` is this campaign's own HOST wall clock at the moment it began; `observedUnixSeconds` is what the CLUSTER's clock said when the crank driver planned. A validator whose clock had been moved to make a deadline pass would report a second outside the interval the campaign itself occupied, and the whole ladder rests on a wall-clock comparison (`SourceResolutionStateV2::crank_recovery_ladder` refuses while `current_unix_seconds <= due`), so a campaign that could warp its own clock could not honestly assert its own hostile.

witnesses.query: if ([.cranks[] | select(.outcome == "executed") | select(.observedUnixSeconds <= .dueUnixSeconds)] | length) == 0 and ([.cranks[] | select(.outcome == "not-yet-due") | select(.observedUnixSeconds > .dueUnixSeconds)] | length) == 0 then "consistent" else "inconsistent" end
witnesses.provenance: `SourceResolutionStateV2::crank_recovery_ladder` refuses while `current_unix_seconds <= due`, so the last second at which an honest observation may still land and the first second at which a crank may run are DIFFERENT seconds. That single conjunct is what stops the funded failure walk from being a shortcut around a leg the market's holders paid for, and it is asserted in both directions here: nothing that executed stood on or before its deadline, and nothing reported as not-yet-due was actually past it.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select((.label | test("refuse"; "i")) | not)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The successor campaign this tier drives submits deliberate expected-failure transactions -- 'Found37 refuses a substituted Market coordinate and rolls the transaction back' is one -- and every one of them SAYS SO in its own label, which is the campaign's own convention and not this tier's. So a finalized transaction carrying a structured InstructionError whose label does not say it refuses is an UNPLANNED refusal, and this counts them. It is not a claim that nothing refused; it is a claim that nothing refused by surprise.

witnesses.query: . as $run | if ($run.publications | length) > 0 and ([$run.publications[] | select(.publishTime >= $run.started_unix_seconds and .publishTime <= $run.finished_unix_seconds)] | length) == ($run.publications | length) then "minted-inside-the-run" else "minted-outside-the-run" end
witnesses.provenance: The publication is the one artifact this tier AUTHORS, so it is the one a reader has most reason to distrust. Its instant is the CLUSTER's own block time, and `started_unix_seconds`/`finished_unix_seconds` are this campaign's own HOST wall clock -- two independent clocks again, exactly as `no-clock-was-warped` uses them. A publication stamped outside the interval the campaign occupied would be one minted about a period the chain was not living through, which is the same defect as moving the validator's clock and is caught the same way. It also says the mint is a producer and not a fixture: a frozen capture could never satisfy this.

The journey's conservation ledger (`tools/gauntlet/journey/src/ledger.rs`), linked rather than reimplemented, evaluating laws L1-L8 at every stage boundary of this walk: after the founding, after each crank, and -- on the capture walk -- after the capture and after the terminal admission. Both walks are censused, which is why this witness is one of the arm-independent ones and is evaluated against each arm’s own transcript in turn. Every account the walk touches -- the market's compartments, the Resolution funding subset ledger, the certificate seats, the provider's own accounts and the stranger who cranks -- is registered BEFORE the first census, so a boundary that reports a green has a predecessor to difference against; a boundary that admitted a new account reports `inapplicable` and names it. A violated law is a lamport or an atom this walk cannot account for, and zero is the only value that says the ladder moved a market rather than merely a set of accounts.

`drive_crank` in `tools/gauntlet/ladder/src/ladder.rs` distinguishes two refusals of the shipped `dclutch-successor-bootstrap recovery-crank` driver and treats them oppositely on purpose. A refusal carrying `a crank is admissible STRICTLY after the deadline` is the tier's own HOSTILE satisfied and the walk goes on; every other preflight refusal is a real stop, recorded as `refused-in-preflight` with the driver's sentence verbatim, and the arm returns having built no frame at all. Zero is the only value that says every crank this walk reports was a crank the driver was willing to build -- and a nonzero one is also why `every-crank-frame-is-the-relay-contract-eighteen` would read an empty width, since a refused preflight has no frame to count.
